newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end sharply lower.

text.p: French stocks fell sharply on Tuesday on profit-taking fuelled by Wall Street's drop and caution ahead of the new Socialist-led government's keynote policy speech on Thursday.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 33.27 points, or 1.19 percent, at 2,762.60 points. The CAC-40 June futures contract fell 42 points to 2,743 points.
Sentiment on the bourse was cooling after a Monday morning surge to all-time highs, and investors were starting to feel cautious ahead of Prime Minister Lionel Jospin's policy speech.
"We rose after the Socialists' victory without even knowing their programme. We could end up very disappointed," a broker said.
Contradictory interpretations of the compromise agreement struck in Amsterdam by EU leaders on Monday also weighed on the market by signalling a rocky road to European monetary union.
A consolidation could take the bourse's CAC-40 index to 2,650 points, some traders said.
Trading was calmer on Tuesday than in recent sessions, but big block trades swelled volume to 7.52 billion francs.

Two blocks of 655,000 and 103,000 shares in Alcatel Alsthom were traded, and two blocks of 422,000 and 111,000 shares in Elf Aquitaine were traded. A block of 72,224 shares in Club Mediterranee was also traded.
* Primagaz closed down 3.80 percent on the placement of 3.77 percent of its capital held by Mobil at 530 francs per share.
* Insurance firm GAN rose 3.28 percent, bolstered by persistent merger speculation.
